sections.content: Use expressions such as *creo* *que*, pienso que, me *parece* que and *desde* mi *punto* de *vista* to introduce an opinion. When giving a reason, connect the opinion to a second clause rather than leaving it as an isolated statement.

items.spanish: Creo que esta propuesta es útil porque responde a un problema real.
items.english: I think this proposal is useful because it responds to a real problem.

items.spanish: Desde mi punto de vista, la medida debería cambiar, ya que afecta a muchas personas.
items.english: From my point of view, the measure should change, since it affects many people.

items.spanish: Me parece que esta postura es razonable, aunque necesita más evidencia.
items.english: It seems to me that this position is reasonable, although it needs more evidence.

items.spanish: Considero que debemos escuchar otros puntos de vista antes de decidir.
items.english: I consider that we should listen to other points of view before deciding.

sections.content: Me *parece* *que* works impersonally — it literally 'seems to me', not 'I seem' — even though it functions exactly like *creo* *que*. Both take the indicative here, since neither one doubts or negates the claim.
